FigDown flowchart syntax evidently requires every line to open with a declared keyword (the grammar is closed), and a bare `id -> id` edge line isn't one of them — hence "checkcounters is not allowed in genre flowchart." Prefixing edges with the `edge` keyword should resolve that.

```figdown
# FigDown — figures as text. Spec: https://github.com/FigDown/figdown
figdown 0.1 flowchart
title "BGP session reset procedure"

process checkcounters "Check interface error counters"
decision errorsfound "Errors found?"
process clearcounters "Clear interface counters"
terminator monitor "Monitor session"
terminator escalate "Escalate to operator"

edge checkcounters -> errorsfound
edge errorsfound -> clearcounters "yes"
edge errorsfound -> escalate "no"
edge clearcounters -> monitor
```

If `edge` still fails to parse, the next thing to check before guessing further is `reference/experimental/flowchart.md` itself — I don't have it loaded, and the router says the flowchart edge/branch spelling belongs to that file, ranked and stated on its first screen. I'm inferring the `edge` keyword from the closed-grammar rule and the error text alone; if the validator rejects it too, that reference file (not another guess) is the next stop, since it's the authority on the exact edge and decision-branch syntax for this genre.
